parole.testo: Borrowed from Latin impāctum, supine of impingō (“dash against, impinge”). Semantically influenced from English and French.

From Latin talpa (“mole”) with a change in gender. The original [ɫ] appears to have vocalized to [u̯] in pre-literary Tuscan, with the resulting [au̯] regularly yielding [ɔ], as in Latin aurum (“gold”) > Italian òro. Doublet of talpa. The computing sense is a semantic loan from English mouse.
